paras: I grew up in Windhoek, Namibia, and now live in Eislingen/Fils near Stuttgart. I'm training as a Fachinformatiker für Systemintegration — an IT systems integration specialist — and since September 2026 I'm in my second training year at IT-Works GmbH in Uhingen.

My first year at netplay GmbH put me straight into client work: Proxmox servers and backups, OPNsense firewalls, Windows rollouts, patch automation and the daily support queue. At home I run a three-node Proxmox lab where I try things out before I'd ever touch them on a production system.
Before IT I competed in artistic gymnastics at Level 8 and coached kids in Windhoek. I still fly drones and enjoy taking old hardware apart to see how it works.

projects.label: Projects
projects.intro: Six things I built or fixed, written the way an IHK project report is structured: starting point, what I did, result.

items.title: Central Windows patching with AWX
items.situation: Windows 11 clients and VMs were updated by hand, one machine at a time — slow, and easy to forget one.
items.action: Installed AWX (the web UI for Ansible), built inventories, connected Windows hosts over WinRM and wrote job templates and playbooks. Tested everything in a lab before rolling it out.
items.result: Updates for several Windows machines run from one place, repeatably and with a log of every run.

items.title: Infrastructure documentation for two client sites
items.situation: Two small-business clients had no complete, current documentation of their servers and network.
items.action: Collected data read-only from production Proxmox (qm, pvesm, pvesh) and OPNsense: VMs, IPs, storage, VPN, DHCP leases, firewall and NAT rules. Turned it into structured Excel, PDF and JSON files.
items.result: Handover-ready documentation for both sites. On the way I found a full swap partition and a VM on a disabled storage and reported both.

items.title: Active Directory lab on VMware ESXi
items.situation: I wanted to understand Windows domains properly before working on them at a client.
items.action: Built a domain controller on Windows Server 2025 with OUs and groups, file shares with share and NTFS permissions, GPO drive mappings, and an OPNsense VM for DHCP and DNS — isolated on its own vSwitches.
items.result: A reproducible lab I can reset any time. Key lesson: when share and NTFS rights meet, the more restrictive one wins.

items.title: Local AI stack on old server hardware
items.situation: I wanted private AI tools at home — on a Xeon without AVX2 and no big GPU.
items.action: Built a dedicated LLM VM with llama.cpp behind llama-swap (eight models), LibreChat as the front end with SearXNG web search, and a Hermes Agent reachable via WhatsApp. Tuned flash attention, mlock and a quantised KV cache, and fixed a disk layout that left most of the disk unused.
items.result: Stable 7–8 tokens per second on CPU, fully local, no cloud dependency.

items.title: Phishing simulation for security awareness
items.situation: A client wanted to find out how its staff react to a realistic phishing e-mail.
items.action: Built the landing page and the e-mail for a controlled simulation and tested the whole flow before launch.
items.result: A ready-to-run awareness campaign — and a much better eye of my own for what makes phishing convincing.

items.title: DrehBAR — a cocktail machine in Python
items.situation: Vocational-school project: control a cocktail machine with a rotating tray.
items.action: Wrote the mixing logic in Python with an SQLite recipe database, tray-rotation logic, timed dispensing with fill-level tracking and animated tkinter progress bars. Added documentation and a test protocol.
items.result: Working software with documentation, delivered as a team project.

homelab.flow_desc: Diagram: internet traffic enters through OPNsense and is routed to three Proxmox nodes. Node 1 runs Nginx Proxy Manager, Pi-hole, Vaultwarden, Beszel, Paperless-ngx and PBS. Node 2 runs the LLM VM, LibreChat, Hermes Agent, Ollama and Firecrawl. Node 3 runs n8n, BookStack, WordPress, Anubis and RustDesk.
